items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: And a fellow by the name of Buzzy Willards playing banjo. A fellow by the name of Bill Gillen playing trumpet.

ctx.x: Can you just mention a few of the names?

Oh, yes. I remember, for sure, they had... Broken Dishes. Von Gammon. Oh, well, he's talking about my girlfriend now. Broken... I'm just kidding. She could have been. Broken Dishes, who really used to be a real tough girl. She used to beat up all the other girls, you know. She was tattooed. She was tattooed from head to foot. You know, the girls were working on tickets, you know. They'd try to beat one another out of dances, and she'd go back in, and she'd have it out with them. But it was all really part of the…

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: The only time that I had ever played with Bill was at the Fern Dance Hall.

ctx.x: And what other bands did Gillen play with that you know of?

I don't know of any other bands that he played with, Dick. The only time that I had ever played with Bill was at the Fern Dance Hall. After I left the Fern Dance Hall, I'd like to mention that I went to my first nightclub job, or cabaret they called it in the old days, was the Valencia on Bourbon Street. That was about 1927, I think. And I played with a little outfit there. I believe it was Hilton Lamar's brother, Jimmy Lamar, played alto sax. And Chink Martin's son, Chink Junior, played banjo. Buck Rogers played…
I wonder where he got his style. I can't imagine.
